artist.name: Taylor Swift
artist.bio: Taylor Alison Swift is an American singer-songwriter. An influential figure in popular culture, Swift is known for her autobiographical songwriting and artistic reinventions. She is the highest-grossing live music artist, the wealthiest female musician, and one of the best-selling music artists of all time.

eras.name: The Life of a Showgirl
eras.blurb: Orange feathers, full theatre. The loudest, most glitter-forward era yet.

eras.name: THE TORTURED POETS DEPARTMENT
eras.blurb: Announced live at the Grammys. Thirty-one tracks by 2am, because of course there was an anthology.

eras.name: Midnights
eras.blurb: Thirteen sleepless nights. Out at midnight, then again at 3am with seven more songs, then again as the Til Dawn Edition with You're Losing Me — the only non-Taylor's-Version album she kept expanding after release.

eras.name: evermore
eras.blurb: folklore's sister record, out five months later. Autumn, braids, and a plait down her back.

eras.name: folklore
eras.blurb: Written in lockdown, announced sixteen hours before it came out. Grey cardigans and imaginary people.

eras.name: Lover
eras.blurb: Pastel skies, glitter hearts, and the one where the cats really take over. The rainbow era.

eras.name: reputation
eras.blurb: After the 1989 high came Kanye, Kim and a tabloid pile-on that pulled her all the way back down. She disappeared — not just from press during the cycle, but from public life before it. "There will be no explanation. There will just be reputation." Her first album as co-producer.

Full pop, no apologies. Polaroids, New York, and the biggest sales week she'd had. She was single, leaning into the serial-heartbreak image the press had built for her, and putting her friendships front and centre instead. People still call it the modern pop bible.

eras.name: Red
eras.blurb: The heartbreak record, and the one where country starts giving way to pop — Max Martin and Shellback turn up and the edges change shape. All Too Well is here, though the ten-minute version wouldn't arrive until Taylor's Version in 2021.

eras.name: Speak Now
eras.blurb: Written entirely alone, no co-writers, as an answer to people who said she didn't write her own songs.

eras.name: Fearless
eras.blurb: The one that made her the youngest person ever to win Album of the Year. Gold dress, spinning in a field.

eras.name: Taylor Swift
eras.blurb: Seventeen, curly hair, a guitar with rhinestones on it. She wrote or co-wrote every track.

cats.name: Olivia Benson
cats.namedAfter: Detective Olivia Benson, Law & Order: SVU
cats.caption: the actual star of this family
cats.note: Appears in the Blank Space video, the ME! video, and a Diet Coke ad. Has been valued at around $97 million on lists of the world's richest pets, which is a real sentence about a cat.

cats.name: Meredith Grey
cats.caption: hates having her picture taken
cats.note: The eldest and the most private. She largely retired from public life around 2019, which fans took roughly as hard as a breakup.

cats.name: Benjamin Button
cats.namedAfter: The Curious Case of Benjamin Button
cats.caption: the baby, and he knows it
cats.note: Picked up on the set of the ME! video and kept. There is footage of the exact moment she decides to keep him, and it is worth watching.

timeline.title: Taylor Swift
timeline.body: Debut album at 16. Country radio didn't quite know what to do with a teenager writing her own songs about actual teenagers.

timeline.title: Fearless
timeline.body: Won Album of the Year at the Grammys and made her the youngest artist ever to do it. She was 20.

timeline.title: Speak Now
timeline.body: Every track written alone. It was a direct answer to people questioning whether she wrote her own material.

timeline.title: Red
timeline.body: The pivot out of country. Also the album that later gave everyone the ten-minute All Too Well.
Fully pop. Sold 1.28 million copies in its first week and won Album of the Year.

timeline.title: reputation
timeline.body: No interviews, no press, all snake. The tour became the highest-grossing US tour of its year.

timeline.title: Lover
timeline.body: Pastels and hearts after all that black. Also the year she began speaking publicly about owning her masters.

timeline.title: folklore
timeline.body: Announced sixteen hours before release, written in lockdown. Won Album of the Year, her third.

timeline.title: evermore
timeline.body: A second surprise album in the same year, five months after the first.

timeline.title: The re-recordings begin
timeline.body: Fearless (Taylor's Version) arrives — the first of the re-recorded albums, made to own her own masters.

timeline.title: Midnights
timeline.body: Thirteen sleepless nights. Then a 3am edition with seven more songs, three hours later.

timeline.title: The Eras Tour begins
timeline.body: A three-and-a-half hour set spanning every era. It became the highest-grossing tour in history.

timeline.title: THE TORTURED POETS DEPARTMENT
timeline.body: Announced live while accepting a Grammy. Thirty-one tracks once the anthology dropped at 2am.

timeline.title: She buys her masters back
timeline.body: Announced in a letter on her site. After six years and four re-recorded albums she buys the originals outright from Shamrock Capital and owns her entire catalogue.

timeline.title: Engaged
timeline.body: Travis Kelce proposes in a garden in Lee's Summit, Missouri. She posts it to Instagram on 26 August.

timeline.title: Songwriters Hall of Fame
timeline.body: Inducted at 36 — the youngest woman ever, and second-youngest overall behind Stevie Wonder. She'd taken the Hal David Starlight Award in 2010, making her the first to graduate from that to full membership. The speech ran about twenty minutes.

timeline.title: Married
timeline.body: She and Travis Kelce marry at Madison Square Garden. Adam Sandler officiates; their brothers stand as best man and man of honour.

facts: Her lucky number is 13. She was born on the 13th, turned 13 on Friday the 13th, and used to paint it on her hand before shows.
She wrote the whole of Speak Now by herself — no co-writers on any track.
Olivia Benson the cat has appeared on lists of the world's wealthiest pets with an estimated value around $97 million.
folklore and evermore were both written and released in 2020, five months apart, with no advance warning.
The Eras Tour is the highest-grossing concert tour ever staged, and the first to pass $1 billion.
She re-recorded her first six albums to own the masters, then bought the originals back outright in 2025.

All Too Well came out of a Speak Now tour rehearsal, improvised on the spot. Accounts of how long that original ran vary from ten minutes to twenty; it was cut to five for Red, and the full ten-minute version finally arrived with Red (Taylor's Version) in 2021.
She re-recorded four of the six albums — Fearless, Red, Speak Now and 1989. reputation and the debut never got a Taylor's Version, because she bought the originals back first.
Her Instagram comments are switched off.
She has won Album of the Year at the Grammys four times, more than any other artist.
Benjamin Button was picked up on the set of the ME! video and simply never left.
She has said she reads the comments, which is either brave or a warning depending on how you look at it.
